scope.description: Original staged snapshot: 767 insertions and 1 deletion; excludes subsequent owner fixes.

intent: Implement versioned reversible fleet audit/setup/rollback and trusted-worktree noninteractive agent launch with bounded Git and permission checks. Preserve credentials, unrelated WIP, managed policy, and branch protections; report actual blocked states and exact-ref Git delivery evidence.

evidence: AGENTS.md:32-37 requires SandboxRuntimeService and its verified wm-<repo>-<owner>-<suffix> namespace; fleet_permissions.py:327-339 instead launches and stops a pf83 container directly.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the Docker runtime launch, inspection, and timeout cleanup into `SandboxRuntimeService` (extending it for this pinned image/auth bind if necessary), and have FleetProfile call that service using its verified `wm-<repo>-<owner>-<suffix>` ownership convention.
findings.title: Route Docker launch through sandbox runtime
findings.why_it_matters: Direct Docker launch and cleanup bypass SandboxRuntimeService, its ownership verification, and the required wm-<repo>-<owner>-<suffix> namespace.
findings.validation_reason: When the new Docker launch path runs, fleet_permissions.py:327-339 creates and stops its own pf83 container directly instead of using SandboxRuntimeService and its ownership convention, contradicting AGENTS.md:32-37; the dispatch path is explicit in the new code, although operational incidence was not measured.

evidence: fleet_permissions.py:154-160 omits host managed policy mounts; :279-280 labels policy enforced, while :289-301 does not require equivalent container policy. Validator in-memory probe returned PASS despite reported host requirements and no policy mount.
findings.suggested_fix: Fail Docker preflight when host Codex managed policy is present until equivalent enforcement inside the selected image is verified. Alternatively bind the applicable requirements and managed configuration read-only at their supported container locations and let conflicting danger-full-access/approval flags block launch; do not label policy enforced based only on host file existence. Add a negative fixture with requirements forbidding danger-full-access.
findings.title: CWE-284 Docker launch drops host-managed Codex policy
findings.why_it_matters: A host policy forbidding full access can pass preflight while the container omits that policy and requests danger-full-access. Audit nevertheless reports CLI_ENFORCED_NOT_OVERRIDDEN; filesystem isolation does not preserve the missing approval, network, command, or feature restrictions.
findings.validation_reason: For a host with local Codex requirements and an image lacking equivalent policy, fleet_permissions.py:154-160 omits those files while requesting danger-full-access and :289-301 never gates their absence, consistent with the documented local policy locations (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/managed-configuration#locations-and-precedence); an independent in-memory probe of the frozen source returned PASS with host requirements reported present and no policy mount, while operational incidence was not measured.

evidence: fleet_permissions.py:176-181 checks only POSIX UID APIs; scripts/fleet-permissions.py:7-10 invokes main directly, bypassing Windows checks in scripts/fleet-permissions.ps1:12-16. Validator identity probe without UID APIs passed.
findings.suggested_fix: Move Windows elevation and workspace-owner validation into a shared core guard called by identity/apply/check/launch, using the Windows process token and ACL owner SID; fail closed when these checks cannot run. Keep the PowerShell checks as early diagnostics rather than the only enforcement, and cover direct Python entry from elevated and foreign-owned-workspace fixtures.
findings.title: CWE-284 Windows Python entry bypasses ownership and elevation guards
findings.why_it_matters: Direct Windows Python entry skips POSIX-only UID checks, allowing elevated or foreign-owned writable worktrees to reach trust and launch. The optional PowerShell wrapper is the only Windows enforcement.
findings.validation_reason: On direct Windows Python entry with an elevated process or writable foreign-owned worktree, fleet_permissions.py:176-181 skips both POSIX-only checks and scripts/fleet-permissions.py:7-10 never invokes the PowerShell guards at :12-16; an independent in-memory identity probe without UID APIs passed, while actual Windows incidence was not measured.

evidence: fleet_gh.py:36-42 creates the final binary before the receipt and symlink; :61-62 makes rollback a no-op without a receipt. Reviewer failure-injection fixture observed the leftover binary, absent receipt, failed retry, and unchanged rollback.
findings.suggested_fix: Journal or stage installation before publishing final artifacts, recover matching partial files on retry or rollback, and clean up only newly created files when later steps fail. Add receipt-write and symlink-write failure tests that verify retry and rollback recover while preserving conflicting files.
findings.title: Interrupted gh setup cannot retry or roll back
findings.why_it_matters: Failure writing the receipt leaves a binary that blocks retry with FileExistsError. Rollback sees no receipt and reports unchanged, violating reversible, idempotent setup.
findings.validation_reason: If receipt writing fails after binary creation, fleet_gh.py:36-42 leaves the final binary without a receipt, the next invocation reaches O_EXCL again, and rollback at :61-62 returns unchanged, violating the new idempotent setup requirement; the exception path is reachable through an unwritable state directory, though its incidence was not measured.

evidence: fleet_permissions.py:262-263 queries an HTTPS credential helper; :289-290 requires it for every launch. Validator preflight probe reproduced this sole blocker with all other checks passing.
findings.first_evidence: app/services/fleet_permissions.py:263 --         checks["git_helper"] = {"code": "CONFIGURED" if helper.returncode == 0 and helper.stdout.strip() else "AUTH_REQUIRED"}
findings.suggested_fix: Keep credential.helper as diagnostic information and gate Git authentication using a bounded noninteractive probe of the actual configured origin through GitWorkspaceService. Classify its real transport failure, and retain the separate task-owned write canary for proof of push permission; do not require an HTTPS helper for SSH remotes.
findings.title: SSH Git authentication is rejected without HTTPS credential helper
findings.why_it_matters: A working SSH origin is blocked when an HTTPS credential helper is absent, even with valid GitHub CLI authentication and push permission.
findings.validation_reason: For a working SSH origin without an HTTPS credential helper, fleet_permissions.py:262-263 produces AUTH_REQUIRED and :289-290 unconditionally blocks it despite GitWorkspaceService supporting noninteractive SSH at :26; an independent in-memory preflight probe reproduced that sole blocker with every other required check passing, while fleet incidence was not measured.

evidence: git_workspace.py:128-134 implements mismatch and failed-cleanup paths; repository-wide test inspection found only the success-path push_canary call at tests/test_fleet_permissions.py:100-112.
findings.suggested_fix: Add focused push_canary tests that simulate a different ls-remote SHA and a failed deletion/absence check; assert code remains BLOCKED, cleanup stays NOT_RUN, and the created worktree and remote ref are retained. Keep the existing real-bare-remote success test for the normal delivery proof.
findings.title: Canary recovery branches lack tests
findings.why_it_matters: The sole canary test covers success. It cannot catch deletion of evidence or worktrees after SHA mismatch or cleanup failure, despite the exact-ref recovery guarantee.
findings.validation_reason: The newly added mismatch and failed-cleanup paths at git_workspace.py:128-134 require remote SHA divergence or deletion/absence failure, but repository-wide test inspection found only the success-path push_canary call in tests/test_fleet_permissions.py:100-112, confirming the specific missing recovery coverage without asserting an observed production failure.

evidence: git_workspace.py:125-131 separates SHA readback from unconditional deletion; :132-138 can report PASS after deleting a newer tip, contradicting the preservation contract at :104.
findings.suggested_fix: Make remote cleanup an atomic compare-and-delete against the recorded canary SHA. If the available Git mechanism would violate the explicit no-force policy, fail closed by retaining the remote ref and reporting cleanup BLOCKED with the branch and expected SHA, rather than issuing an unconditional deletion. Add a fixture that advances the ref after readback and verifies the newer tip survives.
findings.title: Concurrent ref advancement is deleted by canary cleanup
findings.why_it_matters: Another writer can advance the remote ref between readback and unconditional deletion. Cleanup then deletes the newer tip and reports PASS.
findings.validation_reason: If another writer advances the unique canary ref after readback and before the deletion push connects, git_workspace.py:125-131 has no atomic expected-SHA condition and :132-138 can report PASS after deleting that newer tip, contrary to :104; the ordering is permitted by the two separate Git operations, although concurrent incidence was not measured.

evidence: terminal_launcher.py:83-95 implements the entry point; repository-wide test inspection found no calls to it. tests/test_fleet_permissions.py:85-89 exercises FleetProfile.launch only.
findings.suggested_fix: Add TerminalLauncherService tests with injected FleetProfile/preflight and popen fakes: assert a blocked gate returns dispatched false and never invokes _launch, and a passing gate invokes the fleet-permissions.py launch command with the validated workspace, agent, prompt-file, and supplied --state.
findings.title: Trusted terminal launch lacks integration coverage
findings.why_it_matters: Tests never call launch_trusted_agent, so they do not verify blocked preflight prevents terminal dispatch or passing preflight forwards the validated workspace, prompt, agent, and state.
findings.validation_reason: For calls to the new launch_trusted_agent entry with blocked or passing preflight, terminal_launcher.py:83-95 supplies the security gate and runner arguments, but repository-wide inspection found no test calling this entry and tests/test_fleet_permissions.py:85-89 exercises only FleetProfile.launch, confirming the stated integration coverage gap without asserting a current gate bypass.

triage_groups.title: Docker policy and lifecycle enforcement
triage_groups.context: Decision gate: integrate Docker ownership and policy enforcement through the required sandbox service.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Enforce managed policy for #2 and integrate that enforcement into the owned sandbox runtime for #1.
triage_groups.why: One container launch path should preserve policy and use the required ownership-aware lifecycle.

triage_groups.title: Exact-ref canary recovery
triage_groups.context: Decision gate: choose conditional cleanup compatible with the no-force policy, or retain the ref and report BLOCKED.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Fix the conditional cleanup behavior in #7, then add the failed-readback and failed-deletion coverage in #6.
triage_groups.why: The safety invariant and recovery tests cover the same destructive operation.

testing_gaps.gap: The sole canary test covers success. It cannot catch deletion of evidence or worktrees after SHA mismatch or cleanup failure, despite the exact-ref recovery guarantee.
Tests never call launch_trusted_agent, so they do not verify blocked preflight prevents terminal dispatch or passing preflight forwards the validated workspace, prompt, agent, and state.
